"""Linearizability checker for atomic range transactions.

A whole transaction is one atomic operation.  We must decide whether the
completed history admits a serial order (witness) that

  * respects real time (A.end <= B.start  =>  A before B), and
  * reproduces every observed return value when transactions are executed
    one after another from `initial`, ending exactly at `final`.

Search: depth first over topological orders, carrying the map produced by the
prefix.  Failures are memoised on (set-of-placed-transactions, map) because the
future depends on exactly that pair.  A cheap but strong prune uses the target
map: whenever a key currently differs from its required final value, some still
unscheduled transaction must be able to write that required value (otherwise the
final map can never be reached again).
"""

import json
import sys

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- interpreters

def run(prog, state):
    """Execute one transaction on `state` (tuple).  Return new tuple or None
    when an expected observation does not match."""
    st = list(state)
    for ins in prog:
        c = ins[0]
        if c == 1:                                   # put
            st[ins[1]] = ins[2]
        elif c == 0:                                 # get
            if st[ins[1]] != ins[2]:
                return None
        elif c == 2:                                 # del
            st[ins[1]] = None
        elif c == 3:                                 # cas
            i = ins[1]
            ok = st[i] == ins[2]
